title: Take a Good Look
dateline: The bay road cut, below the Academy.
mood: On the wet stones of the cut, Guinevere looks up at someone she thought she knew.

hero.alt: Close on Guinevere's face in a dark street, a smudge on her cheek, her eyes narrowed as she looks up.

segs.t: Guinevere lay on wet stones and could not get her breath back. Something in her side stabbed each time she tried.
When the light went out of her drones, she had fallen. An awning, then the street. Somewhere between the two her earpiece had gone, and the channel with it.
Both drones lay beside her, gray and dark. Her wings were gone. She reached for her power the way she always did, and nothing came.
Vexana knelt over her. In the orb of her staff no light burned.
“Up,” said Vexana. “Slowly.”
Her arm slid under Guinevere’s shoulders.
“One,” said Guinevere. The stab came again. “Two. Three.”
She was still on the stones.
“Four,” said Vexana, and lifted.
On four Guinevere was sitting up against her, breathing in small pieces.
“Sitting counts,” she said.
“It doesn’t.”

They were at the mouth of the bay road cut. A short way up the narrow street, where the houses stood closest, Fanny was building a wall. A door, a shop sign, a car tipped onto its side. Layla and a few Shield soldiers dragged and stacked. In the middle Fanny left one gap, wide enough to let one Ender through at a time.
Past the wall the street climbed to the shelters, full now. At the top Angela knelt among the wounded, and Ruby stood over them.
Over the bay road the slabs still hung in the air, turning in the rain.
Guinevere’s hand went to her collar. Two fingers, the way they had gone every morning of the search.
The star was cold.
For weeks it had been the only proof she had. Lit meant Vexana was out there somewhere. She had never once let herself picture it dark.
Dark,
she thought.
And here she is anyway.
Down on the bay road the smoke parted, and four Enders stepped through. They were taller than the morning’s, on long jointed legs, like spiders standing up. They came on toward the mouth of the cut.
Vexana’s arm tightened. “Up. Again.”
Something dropped out of the sky and landed between the Enders and the two of them.
It hit the stones in a crouch, and the stones cracked. Lightning ran off it into the puddles and died there.

It was a girl. Dark plate trimmed with silver was still closing over her, up her ribs and over her throat. Pale shards of armor stood up off her shoulders. A long cloak hung down her back, purple running into blue.
She straightened. The four Enders came up close behind her on their long legs. None of them reached for her.
Guinevere had seen that once already today, on the platform, around Vexana.
A lollipop stick stood out of the corner of the girl’s mouth.
Guinevere knew the stick before she knew the face. Then she knew the face.

Blonde hair, and two small horns standing up out of it. Guinevere had seen those horns in class every day, in front of a dark headband, and taken them for part of it. The headband was gone. The horns grew out of her hair.
The rest was new. Ears that came to points. Hands that ended in black claws.
“Selena?”
Selena came toward her, and the Enders came on behind. She stopped over the two of them and looked down at Guinevere. She did not look at the wall.
When she smiled, she showed fangs.
Selena lifted one hand and laid the tips of her claws against her cheek, just under one red eye.
“Take a good look. This is the real me.”

blocks.caption: Take a good look. This is the real me.

segs.t: Nobody laughed.
On the Academy stairs everybody had. A boy had called her dangerous, and Selena had waved her lollipop over her shoulder without turning.
One day, when the haze clears...
Guinevere had laughed loudest, her head thrown back.
She told us,
thought Guinevere.
She told all of us.

media.alt: Guinevere kneels on the stones among her fallen, sparking drones; then, in a smoky ruined street, Selena walks forward in dark armor and a long purple cloak, tall Enders on jointed legs standing behind her, and lifts a clawed hand to her face.

segs.t: Behind her, at the wall, Layla’s voice had lost all its edge.
Steel scraped. Fanny’s blades had come up.
Against Guinevere’s shoulder, Vexana had gone very still. Guinevere knew that stillness. She had seen it once over a star clip at a shop counter, and Vexana had said nothing then either.
Guinevere looked up at Selena.
The front row. In late every morning with her guardian’s note, her dragon-shaped machine clicking at her heel. Asleep on her arms while the lesson went on. This morning, her papers flying:
what about my graduation?!
Guinevere had always liked her a little. She liked anyone who did not care what a room thought of them.
Her hand lay on an Ender’s robe. Vexana was inside it.
Vexana wears their shape,
she thought.
And Vexana is ours.
So she looked at Selena the way she had looked at Vexana on the platform. Past the plate and the claws, for the girl inside. She did not look away.
Selena’s claws came away from her cheek. Her smile went.
For a breath there was no smile on her face at all. Guinevere had seen her grin in class and yawn through whole lessons. She had never seen this face. She had no name for what was in it.
That’s you,
thought Guinevere.
Then the smile was back.
Lightning broke white over the street. In its glare, smoke rolled up off the wet stones between them. When it thinned, Selena was gone. Rain fell on the cracked stones where she had landed.

The Enders charged at Guinevere, all four at once, and the cut was too narrow for them. Their legs tangled at its mouth and scraped along the house fronts. Behind them the rest came up off the bay road.
“Wall!” shouted Fanny.
Vexana hauled her up, and they ran for the gap. Guinevere’s side screamed. Her drones stayed behind on the stones.
One Ender tore loose from the others. It was on them three steps short of the gap.
Vexana got between it and Guinevere, the dark staff up. It did not slow down. Its shoulder knocked her into a doorway.
No drones, no wings. Only her hands.
I had these first,
she thought.
Before any of it.
It swung. She ducked, and its claw tore a shutter off the house behind her. She came up and hit its chest. Her knuckles split. The plates had already shut, and they did not care.
Hands home,
said Hester’s voice, from a dawn years ago, beside a sandbag that hardly swung.
Guinevere brought them home, up to her chin.
From the gap Fanny shouted, “Wait for the swing!”
They don’t strike easily,
Joe had said.
When one does, that is how long you get.
Its chest had opened while she was ducking, and shut before she came up.
It raised its arm again. Its chest plates began to split.
Every part of her wanted to duck. She stepped in instead, under the arm, toward the claw.
The core glowed between the plates. She drove her fist into it with everything she had left. On her arm guard the little black-haired doll jumped on its clip. The core cracked.
The Ender’s legs folded. It came down across the street in front of the gap and blocked half of it.
Vexana was out of the doorway. Her hand closed on Guinevere’s arm. “Back.”
They went back through the gap. There Guinevere turned around.
Fanny stood in the gap with her steel blades raised. She looked at Guinevere’s side, then at her split knuckles. Then she moved to its edge and gave her the middle.
“You saw it,” Fanny called along the wall. “Like that.”
Below them the other three came on, and the rest behind them. To reach the gap they had to climb over the dead one, one at a time.
Vexana stood at Guinevere’s shoulder, the dark staff held across her body like a pole. Weeks among the Enders had taught her how they moved. She watched each one come over the body.
“Left one,” said Vexana. “It’s going to swing.”
Both stars were dark. Between one Ender and the next, Vexana’s fingers found Guinevere’s wrist anyway, and let go.
The left one came over the body. Its arm went up.
Guinevere was already moving.
